## Overview

**Scope:** original English base game, main rulebook **v1.2**, base glossary, official base FAQ and official base Icon Overview. Marine Worlds and optional solo mode are excluded.

In Ark Nova you plan and build a modern, scientifically managed zoo. You build enclosures according to the animals' way of life and support conservation projects to ensure the preservation of animal species. Gathering diverse animals increases the attractiveness of your zoo, advancing you on the **Appeal track** and generating higher revenues; careful stewardship lets you support conservation projects, advancing you on the **Conservation track** with corresponding bonuses. These two tracks progress in **opposite directions**. If your counters meet or cross at the end of your own turn or during a break, final turns begin. Whoever achieves the best combination of appeal and conservation has built the most successful zoo and wins.

Association work in different zoo associations allows you to partner with zoos and universities around the world; together with specialists and sponsors, they help you manage the tasks needed to achieve your goals.

Ark Nova does not play in formal rounds: players simply take turns (clockwise), one turn at a time, until the end of the game is triggered. In between there are **breaks** — administration phases in which you discard down to your hand limit, recall workers, and gain income. On your turn you always perform one action using one of the 5 Action cards displayed below your zoo map; the position (card slot) of the Action card determines how much you can do with that action.

## Components

**Cards**
- 212 Zoo cards: 128 Animal cards, 64 Sponsor cards, 20 Conservation Project cards
- 12 Base Conservation Project cards
- 11 Final Scoring cards
- 20 double-sided Action cards (5 per set: Build, Cards, Animals, Association, Sponsors — each with side I and side II)

**Tiles & tokens**
- 90 standard enclosures in various sizes (1–5 spaces; both sides of a given size are the same shape — occupied side vs. empty side showing the size number)
- 12 special enclosures: 4× Petting Zoo, 4× Reptile House, 4× Large Bird Aviary
- 34 kiosk / pavilion tiles (kiosk and pavilion are opposite sides of the same tile)
- 20 partner zoos, 12 universities, 15 unique buildings
- 9 Bonus tiles
- 70 money tokens, 20 X-tokens
- 8 Venom tokens, 8 Constriction tokens, 8 Multiplier tokens
- 1 Break token

**Boards & mats**
- 1 game board (Zoo card deck and 6-card display, Reputation track, Appeal track, Conservation track, Break track, Bonus spaces)
- 1 Association board
- 8 player mats (zoo maps): 4× Map A (map for first-time players with a starting advantage — easy), 4× Map 0 (more bonus spaces — intermediate), and Maps 1–8 on the reverse sides (advanced, each with an individual special ability)

**Per player color** (black, blue, red, yellow): 3 counters (appeal, conservation, reputation), 25 player tokens, 4 association workers

**Other:** 2 organizers (general supply), 1 glossary, 1 icon overview, rulebook

## Setup

**Global setup**
1. Place the game board in the center. Place the **Break token** on the start space of the Break track corresponding to your player count (e.g., with three players, the space marked 3).
2. Shuffle the 9 **Bonus tiles** and place a random tile face up on each of the **4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8 conservation**. Do not place tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons. Return the remaining 5 tiles to the box (unused).
3. Shuffle the **Zoo cards** into a face-down deck on its board space. Deal 6 face-down cards to the display spaces on the board.
4. Place the 2 organizers next to the board as the general supply.
5. Place the **Association board** next to the game board, leaving room for one row of cards above and one row below.
   - 5a. Place 1 partner zoo of each continent and 1 university of each kind on the spaces provided on the Association board.
   - 5b. Shuffle the **Base Conservation Project cards** and keep them face down next to the board. In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up below the board; otherwise the 3 topmost.
   - 5c. **2-player game only:** take 6 player tokens of an unused color and cover: on the face-up Base Conservation Project cards, the left level on the left card, the middle level on the middle card, and the right level on the right card; and on the Association board, the three spaces in the left column of the donation area. Covered levels/spaces are blocked and cannot be used by either player. **With three or four players, none of these project levels or donation spaces is blocked at setup.**
6. Shuffle the **Final Scoring cards** and place them face down next to the Association board.
7. Randomly determine a start player. Turn order is clockwise.

**Personal setup (each player)**
- **A.** Take a random Map A zoo map and place it that side up (recommended for the first game; all Map A copies are identical). Map 0 suits beginners after the first game. Maps 1–8 (reverse sides) are advanced maps, each with an individual special ability: with these, take 2 random zoo maps and choose 1 of the advanced maps — or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose 1 each in reverse order of play. Return unselected maps to the box. Map A's ability (same for all players): at the beginning of the game, place an empty 3-space enclosure **and a kiosk** on the indicated spaces. The printed kiosk already counts as built; place a kiosk tile over it as a reminder. You may build adjacent to it.
- **B.** Take one set of Action cards (Build, Cards, Animals, Association, Sponsors). Place one card **side I up** under each of the five card slots on your zoo map: the **Animals** card under the leftmost slot (showing 1), the remaining 4 randomly under the other slots.
- **C.** Choose a color and take all its components.
  - **C1.** Place your appeal, conservation, and reputation counters on the first spaces of their tracks. On the **Appeal track**, stagger by turn order: start player on space 0, second player on space 1, third on space 2, fourth on space 3.
  - **C2.** Place 7 player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of your zoo map; keep the rest next to your map for later use.
  - **C3.** Place 1 association worker on the notepad of your zoo map (the active worker) and the remaining 3 lying down on the designated spaces below the notepad.
- **D.** Take 25 money and put it on your notepad.
- **E.** Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and place them next to your zoo map. You may look at them at any time, but keep them hidden from other players.
- **F.** Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4 as hand cards and discard the other 4 to a face-up discard pile on the board. Keep hand cards hidden. (Tip from the rulebook: choose 1–2 Sponsor and 2–3 Animal cards without conditions you cannot fulfill early, ideally matching the Base Conservation Projects on display.)
- **G.** After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

**Map A bonuses:** its seven support-token bonuses, from top to bottom, are snap one display card, build a size-2 standard enclosure free, gain five money, gain one conservation, gain two reputation, gain twelve money and gain three X-tokens. The first four are received immediately when uncovered and again as break income; the last three are one-time. Take a chosen bonus before or after its project's reward. On Map A the second partner zoo upgrades a card, the third hires a worker and the fourth grants two conservation. The second university upgrades a card and the third grants two conservation. Other maps use their printed bonuses.

**University tiles:** your hand limit is **three cards without the hand-limit university, five cards with it**, checked only at breaks. Other universities do not raise or lower that limit.

| University | Research icons | Reputation on acquisition | Hand-limit effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Research university | 2 | 0 | No change; normally 3 |
| Research/reputation university | 1 | 2 | No change; normally 3 |
| Hand-limit university | 0 | 1 | Raises 3 to **5** |

Take printed reputation when acquiring the university. **Only its research icons count as zoo icons; its reputation award and hand-limit symbol are benefits, not additional zoo icons.**

**Your zoo map:** buildings go in the large central area. You may not build on rock and water spaces (some animals need an enclosure next to rock or water). A built-on space is "covered." Spaces with a special icon may not be built on until you upgrade your Build Action card. Some spaces show a **placement bonus**, gained immediately when you cover them. The left edge holds the 7 player tokens used to support conservation projects (each grants a bonus when taken — always immediately, and some again in each break). The bottom has 5 card slots for your Action cards; the number above each slot is that card's strength. The right side has spaces for partner zoos (5 continents exist, but you can partner with a maximum of 4 — the third requires an upgraded Association action) and universities (3 different ones); fill each column bottom-up and take any bonus printed on a space you cover immediately. Workers, money, and X-tokens live on the notepad.

## Turn Structure

**Taking a turn.** You may not do nothing: playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal action. Use the alternative X-token action when you cannot or do not want to execute a regular action.

 On your turn, choose one of your 5 Action cards, shift it lower than the others to show it is in use, and perform its action with the strength of its card slot (1 = far left through 5 = far right; the further right, the more powerful). After completing the action, remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1.

**X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.

**"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

**Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.

**The Break track.** At the start of the game and after each break, the Break token sits on the starting space for your player count. Various actions and card effects advance it toward the end of the track. When it reaches the **last space**, you call a break for everyone: the break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get **1 X-token** for reaching the last space. Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. After the break, the token returns to its starting space.

**Break procedure** (all players, in order):
1. **Hand card limit:** discard cards of your choice down to your hand limit — normally 3, or 5 with a particular university.
2. **Tokens on Action cards:** return any Multiplier, Venom, and/or Constriction tokens on your Action cards to the supply; they no longer have any effect.
3. **Association board:** return all your association workers to your notepad (active again — all tasks are again available at 1 worker). **Restock one tile of each partner-zoo continent and each university kind**, except kinds **already owned by every player**; do not add duplicate available tiles.
4. **Replenish display:** discard the two bottom cards of the display (folders 1 and 2), move the remaining cards down, and refill the display.
5. **Take income** (when multiple players take display cards, **refill the display after each player**; usually simultaneous; if effects require an order, begin with the player who initiated the break — or the affected player closest to them — and proceed clockwise):
   - a. Money according to your zoo's **appeal** (the amount printed next to your counter on the Appeal track; e.g., space 7 pays 11 money).

## Actions

The position of the Action card sets its strength; each card has a stronger side II once upgraded.

### CARDS action
- **Side I:** Advance the Break token **2 spaces** (you do not gain money for this). Then either **draw from the deck** — compare the strength of the slot with the table on the card and draw the indicated number of cards (maximum 3), after which you might have to discard a card from your hand (one just drawn or one already held) — or **snap**: with strength **5 or more**, instead take exactly **1 card of your choice from the display** into your hand, regardless of your reputation. Replenish the display at the end of your turn. There is no in-turn hand limit; you only discard to your limit during breaks.
- **Side II:** Advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw cards from the deck **and/or from within reputation range** (the display up to your Reputation counter), in any order, using the upgraded table on the card (e.g., at strength 5 you take 4 cards and discard 1). The display is not replenished until your turn is complete. Snapping now works from strength **3** (strength above 3 makes no difference to a snap). **On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw; the reputation restriction applies only to the side-II draw option, not snapping.** Upgrading the Cards action also lets you progress **past 9 reputation** on the Reputation track.

**Reputation spaces and rewards:** reputation begins at 1. Each display folder covers these Reputation-track spaces:

| Display folder | Reputation spaces |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2–3 |
| 3 | 4–6 |
| 4 | 7–9 |
| 5 | 10–12 |
| 6 | 13–15 |

At reputation 5 upgrade an Action card; at 8 hire a worker; at 11 gain one conservation; at 12 gain one X-token; at 13 take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; at 14 gain one conservation; at 15 gain one X-token. Each track bonus is received immediately once. Reputation 10 still requires Cards II.

**Reputation track and display:** whenever you increase reputation, advance your counter 1 step. Reaching a space with a bonus grants that bonus immediately, once. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action (reminder icon on space 10 / folder 5). If your counter is on space 15 and you gain more reputation, it stays on 15 and you take **1 appeal per remaining reputation step**. "Within reputation range" = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. After a turn in which display cards were taken: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces from the deck. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

### BUILD action

Place a newly built standard enclosure **empty side up** (yellow border and size number). Each placement-bonus icon covered is awarded immediately **once**; resolve all covered bonuses before the next building. A standard enclosure turning occupied later does not award its covered placement bonus again.

**Buildings available through Build:**

| Building | Footprint / cost | Maximum in one zoo | Minimum Build side |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard enclosure | Size 1–5 / two money per hex | Multiple | I |
| Kiosk or pavilion | Size 1 / two money | Multiple (kiosks obey spacing) | I |
| Petting Zoo | Size 3 / six money | **One** | I |
| Reptile House | Size 5 / ten money | **One** | II |
| Large Bird Aviary | Size 5 / ten money | **One** | II |

The supply has four tiles of each special enclosure for the four players; **each individual zoo may contain only one of each type**.
- **Side I:** Build **exactly 1 building** of your choice, of size up to the action's strength. Pay **2 money per space** (cost = size × 2) into the supply before placing. Available: kiosk (size 1), pavilion (size 1), standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and the Petting Zoo (special enclosure, size 3; maximum 1 per zoo — other buildings can be built more than once).
- **Placement rules:** build adjacent to an existing building (at least 1 edge touching); your **first building** must instead have at least 1 space on a border space of your zoo map. Build only on empty spaces; buildings may not extend beyond the map, overlap buildings, or cover water/rock spaces. Spaces with the restricted icon require the upgraded Build action. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk (at least 2 spaces between kiosks). If you cannot legally build the desired building, you must choose a different building. Build standard enclosures **empty side up** (yellow edge, showing the size); the Petting Zoo is the same on both sides. Covering a placement-bonus space grants that bonus immediately, once. Each pavilion immediately (and only once) increases your zoo's appeal by 1; kiosks grant income in every break; enclosures house animals.
- **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. Newly available: **Large Bird Aviary** and **Reptile House** (special enclosures, both size 5, maximum 1 each per zoo, both sides the same). When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

**Cards draw tables** (strengths above 5 use the strength-5 column):

| Strength | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Side I: draw / then discard | 1 / 1 | 1 / 0 | 2 / 1 | 2 / 0 | 3 / 1 |
| Side II: draw / then discard | 1 / 0 | 2 / 1 | 2 / 0 | 3 / 1 | 4 / 1 |

A required discard may be a newly drawn or previously held hand card.

### ANIMALS action

**Enclosure state on animal admission:**

| Housing | Required empty space | What to do after admitting the animal |
|---|---|---|
| Standard enclosure | One empty enclosure of at least the required size | **Flip the entire enclosure to its occupied side.** It normally houses one animal. |
| Petting Zoo, Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary | At least the animal's indicated number of free special-enclosure spaces | Put that many supply player tokens on the special enclosure; **never flip** it. |

**Special-enclosure capacity:** Petting Zoo has **three spaces**; Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary each have **five spaces**. Each animal fills the number shown in its special-enclosure icon, marked by one supply player token per filled space; several eligible animals may share a special enclosure while their combined requirements fit.

**Animal capacities:** at strengths 1/2/3/4/5+, side I permits 0/1/1/1/2 animals, side II permits **1/1/2/2/2**. At strength 5+ side II also offers the reputation gain below. These are maximum numbers; a legal regular Animals action must play at least one animal.

- **Side I:** Compare the strength of the slot with the table on the card and play up to the indicated number of Animal cards from your hand (side I permits 0/1/1/1/2 animals at strengths 1/2/3/4/5+, so strength 1 needs boosting or another action). For each animal, in order:
  1. **Check conditions** (left side of the card — e.g., a specific partner zoo, animal category, or continent icons). You may only play the card if you fulfill all conditions.
  2. **Pay the cost** (upper-left corner) into the supply. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces the cost by **3 money per continent icon on the card**. Effects that gain you money for playing the animal pay out later — you must be able to pay the full cost first.
  3. **House the animal.** Choose legal housing and meet its capacity and terrain requirements:
     - **Standard enclosure:** any animal except a Petting Zoo animal may go alone into an empty standard enclosure of at least its printed minimum size. Flip the entire enclosure to its occupied side.
     - **Petting Zoo:** Petting Zoo animals go only here.
     - **Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary:** all reptiles and some birds show an alternative special-enclosure requirement. You may choose that housing instead. Put the indicated number of supply player tokens on its free spaces; if not enough free spaces remain, the animal cannot go there. Never flip a special enclosure.
     - **Water and rock:** the animal's required adjacency applies to the chosen enclosure, including a special enclosure. Count distinct adjacent hexes: multiple edges touching one water hex count as only one; a larger water area counts only the hexes actually adjacent. Meet any printed one- or two-space requirement.
  4. **Place the Animal card** next to your zoo map, overlapping so the information at the top edge stays visible.
  5. **Execute effects:** advance your Appeal counter by the amount shown; some animals also give conservation points or reputation. "After finishing" effects wait until the entire Animals action is done; all other effects execute immediately, even before playing another Animal card (likewise effects on other cards triggered by the play). If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.
  - When playing 2 animals, complete all steps for the first (except "after finishing" effects) before the second; you may decline to play a second. Execute "after finishing" effects only after moving the Animals card to slot 1.
- **Side II:** You may also play Animal cards **from the display** within your reputation range, paying an additional cost equal to the folder number the card is on (2 animals may be any mix of hand/display; the display is not replenished until your turn ends). At strength **5 or more**, you may **optionally gain 1 reputation first**, at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to the animals you then play. You may also play animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.

**Animal card layout:** hexagon = minimum standard-enclosure size; adjacent rock/water icons = required adjacent spaces; alternative special enclosure (with spaces occupied) shown beside it; money cost below; extra play conditions lower-left; category and continent icons upper-right (Petting Zoo animals have no continent); appeal gain (plus any conservation/reputation bonuses) lower-right; play effects per the glossary. If an effect refers to an icon that appears on the card itself, that icon counts. Some animals have an **interactive effect**, which can only apply to you if your zoo has **5 or more appeal** (space 5 on the Appeal track is marked as a reminder). Some cards carry a solo-mode replacement effect in a blue box.

**Animal categories (7):** bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bear and Petting Zoo animal are special cases (black icon on white background). Bears are more of a subcategory, mostly combined with the herbivore or predator icon. When the game asks for animal categories it includes bear and Petting Zoo animals unless they are explicitly excluded.

### Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure

Only **immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built**, you may relocate all corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing each animal separately. **The new special enclosure must meet each moved animal’s water/rock adjacency requirements and have enough free capacity.** For each animal:

1. **Empty a standard enclosure:** flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all that animal's requirements, including terrain. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting its size requirement. If none meets even the size, flip none.
2. **Fill the new special enclosure:** add the animal's indicated number of player tokens from your supply to the new special enclosure.

This is a relocation of an existing animal into your new building. **Removing special-enclosure tokens is the separate Release into the Wild procedure**, where an animal leaves your zoo; relocation adds special-enclosure tokens and frees a standard enclosure under the steps above. Relocation is available only at construction, including construction through permitted bonuses.

### ASSOCIATION action
- **Side I:** Perform **exactly one association task**. You need at least 1 active association worker: place it on the chosen task on the Association board. If 1 of your workers is already on that task, you must place **2** workers instead; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot perform it again until after the break. Other players' workers on a task do not matter. Each task has a strength number: your action's strength must be **at least** the task's strength.
- **The tasks:**
  - **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.
  - **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.
  - **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space and **immediately resolve both its covered-space bonus (if any) and the university tile’s own reputation award (if any)**. You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons and are the only way to increase your hand limit to 5.
  - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** choose either to support a conservation project already in play, or to play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately.
    - **New-card sources:** use your hand. With Association II, you may instead use a display card within reputation range and pay its folder number as an additional cost; do not replenish the display until turn end.
    - **Enter play:** put the new card on the leftmost space above the Association board; push existing cards one place right.

Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free.     - **Support procedure:**

    - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
    - **Icon-count** projects: count the icons on the top edge of all your cards — Animal and Sponsor (including the water or rock space requirements, but not the conditions on the left side) — plus your partner zoos and universities. The card itself counts for its own effects; a double icon counts twice. Conservation-project icons do not count as icons in your zoo. Breeding Program projects (123–127) have the same requirement for all three reward spaces: choose any available one.
- **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

### SPONSORS action
- **Side I:** Play **exactly 1 Sponsor card** from your hand: the action's strength must be at least the card's **level**, and you must meet any conditions on the card's left side. Execute its instant effect and/or its recurring effect (if triggered by the card's own icon), then place it next to your zoo map. **OR:** advance the Break token a number of steps equal to the strength and take that much money — you take the full money even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps to reach the final space.
- **Side II:** Play **one or more** Sponsor cards:
  - **Level budget:** action strength **+1** must be at least the sum of all played cards' levels. X-tokens may push strength beyond 5.
  - **Card sources:** use your hand and/or the display within reputation range. Pay each display card's folder number as an additional cost; replenish only at turn end. Sponsors II also permits cards whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
  - **Effect order:** play the cards one after another. Fully execute each card's instant effects before the next; defer its "after finishing" effects until the action is finished.
  - **Money option:** if you instead advance the Break token, take the money **twice**.

**Sponsor card layout:** level in the upper-left corner (with any build-adjacency water/rock requirement beside it); play conditions on the left; the card's own icon in the upper-right corner. A recurring effect appears at the top on a blue background — purple if it is income in every break. A one-off play effect has a yellow background (lower-left); a final-scoring effect has a brown background (lower-right), with a vertical brown strip behind the level as a reminder once cards are overlapped. If a Sponsor card's effect refers to an icon on the card itself, it counts — but only icons in the upper-right corners of cards are used (plus the rock and water icons in the upper-left). Some Sponsor cards place **unique buildings** (from the 15 tiles) into your zoo, subject to any water/rock adjacency shown; a certain minimum reputation is required to play certain Sponsor cards.

### X-TOKEN action (alternative action)
If you cannot or do not want to perform any of the 5 actions, take exactly **1 X-token** instead. You must still select an Action card, move it to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right; the slot's strength and the card's upgrade state are irrelevant. If you already have 5 X-tokens, you cannot perform this action.

## Scoring / Victory Conditions

**During the game.** Your appeal determines your money income each break. The Conservation track has 4 spaces with a one-time effect when you reach or pass them:
- **2 conservation points:** either upgrade one of your Action cards (flip it) or activate an additional association worker (take a lying worker from the lowest space below the notepad onto the notepad). Each player who reaches space 2 gets this choice.
- **5 and 8 conservation points:** take either 5 money or one of the Bonus tiles next to that space. Execute a chosen tile immediately, then remove it from the game. The 5-money option remains even after both Bonus tiles there are gone.
- **10 conservation points:** the first time any player reaches or exceeds 10, **all players** choose and discard one of their Final Scoring cards (face down under the remaining pile). If no one reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.

**End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track. Appeal gained during another player's turn (for example from Polar Bear Exhibit) waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**; if the end is triggered during a break, **all** players take one more turn.

**Final scoring.**
1. Score your Final Scoring card(s) and all your cards with the end-of-game icon. Each Final Scoring card can grant up to 4 additional conservation points (by table or text, counting your universities, the cards in front of you, and their icons); you can never gain more than **4 conservation points from a single Final Scoring card**.
2. Compute Victory Points: look at the scoring area where your Conservation counter is located and find the **lowest Appeal value in that scoring area** — this is your **Target Number**. **Victory Points = your Appeal value − your Target Number.**
3. The player with the highest positive Victory Point total wins. **Tiebreaker:** the tied player who supported the most conservation projects wins (count the player tokens removed from the left side of the zoo map). If still tied, the tied players share the victory.

Note from the rulebook: to have a positive score, your Appeal counter and Conservation counter have to cross one another.

## Special Rules & Edge Cases

- **Reputation cap:** reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action; on space 15, further reputation converts to 1 appeal per step instead.
- **Interactive effects** on Animal cards apply to you only if your zoo has **5 or more appeal**.
- **Full zoo map:** covering every space except water and rock spaces immediately grants 7 appeal (requires the upgraded Build action to reach the restricted spaces; can also trigger from other effects that build in your zoo).
- **Display timing:** whenever you take cards from the display (snap, or upgraded Cards/Animals/Association/Sponsors plays), do not replenish it until your entire turn is complete; then slide cards down folders in order and refill from the deck. **During the break, at step 4 before income**, discard folder 1 and 2 cards, compact the remaining cards and refill the display.
- **Hand size:** unlimited during play; enforced only at breaks (limit 3, or 5 with the specific university).
- **Money-gain timing:** you must be able to pay an animal's full cost before any "gain money" effect from the play pays out.
- **Kiosk spacing** (at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk) applies to every new kiosk, including free ones from card effects (e.g., "Each time you play an Americas icon into your zoo, you may build 1 kiosk for free").
- **Moving animals into a new special enclosure:** allowed only immediately when you build the Reptile House / Large Bird Aviary, once per building. For each animal moved, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all its requirements (including water/rock) back to empty; if none does, use the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none and mark the special enclosure with the suitable number of player tokens; decide per animal.
- **Discarded conservation projects:** tokens on a project card pushed off the display return to the owners' **supply**, not to the bonus spaces on their zoo maps (the bonuses stay activated).
- **2-player game:** one level on each face-up Base Conservation Project and the left column of the donation area are blocked for both players.
- **Multiple simultaneous effects** (appeal, reputation, conservation points, card abilities): the owning player chooses the order of execution.
- **Break trigger from effects:** an Action card, Sponsor card, or Animal card effect can advance the Break token to the last space; the break happens after the current turn ends, the triggering player gains 1 X-token, and extra steps beyond the last space are ignored.
- **Association worker supply:** hire workers from the lowest supply space upward. **Last-worker reward:** certain zoo maps grant **conservation points** when you hire your last worker.
- **Cards that clog:** if you cannot perform any action, the X-token action is always available — unless you already hold 5 X-tokens.
- **Component supply:** if a component runs out, **use a suitable substitute**. Physical stock alone does not forbid an otherwise legal play; explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply. Keep a few standard enclosures and kiosks/pavilions in reserve.

### Base glossary: shared principles

The seven animal categories are **bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal**. Bear can appear alongside herbivore or predator; it remains a category. Petting Zoo animal is its own game category. Include both special categories whenever animal categories are requested, unless explicitly excluded.

**Species Diversity** counts different animal categories in your zoo, not the total number of category icons. Repeated copies of one category do not increase diversity; continent and research icons are not animal categories. Its illustrated levels require 5/4/3 different categories for 5/3/2 conservation respectively; choose a fulfilled, unoccupied level under normal support rules.

**Other illustrated project rewards** (left / middle / right levels; choose any fulfilled, unoccupied level under the normal support rules):

| Project in the main-rule examples | Requirement and reward |
|---|---|
| Reptiles | 5 / 4 / 2 reptile icons give 5 / 4 / 2 conservation. |
| Large Animals | 4 / 3 / 2 large animals give 4 / 3 / 2 conservation. Large means printed standard-enclosure requirement 4–5. |
| Aquatic | The visible outer levels require 5 / 2 water icons for 4 / 2 conservation. The middle reward is 3 conservation; use the card’s printed middle requirement, which is obscured in the supplied illustration. |
| Serengeti National Park | Release one Africa animal with printed standard size 4+ / 3 / 2− for 5 / 4 / 3 conservation. Bringing the project into play also grants 1 reputation; supporting it later does not grant that play bonus. |
| Reptile Breeding Program | Have a reptile and a partner zoo from that reptile’s continent; the same condition applies to all three spaces. Their rewards are **2 conservation + 2 reputation / 1 conservation + 2 reputation / 2 conservation**. Choose any available space. |


**Counting icons in your zoo:**
- **Animal cards and Sponsor cards:** count their upper-right icons. On **Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards**, also count the **water/rock requirements in the upper-left corner**.
- **Partner zoos and universities:** count their continent and research icons. A university’s reputation award and hand-limit mark are benefits, not zoo icons.
- **Do not count:** left-side play conditions or conservation-project icons.
- A card counts its own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. When an effect asks for **different icon types**, repeated copies still represent only one type.

Card text takes priority over general rules. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

A connected space is **uncovered** and shares an edge with a covered space. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. "Your zoo" includes your played cards, map and personal supply; "any zoo" includes these for all players.

For an effect written "X : Y," **X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward**. A condition without a number (or with "per") pays once per fulfillment. A numbered threshold pays only once; with several thresholds use the highest one met. Blue effects are permanent/recurring, purple gives break income, yellow is an instant play benefit and brown is final scoring.

Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor: if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate it freely, but do not flip it. Apply ordinary placement rules and any terrain requirements; no size-based construction payment is due. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and never count as water or rock spaces.

### Base Final Scoring and map clarifications

**Printed scoring tables:** Sponsored Zoo gives 1/2/3/4 conservation for 3/6/8/10 Sponsor cards. Large Animal Zoo gives 1/2/3/4 conservation for 1/2/4/5 large animals (printed standard size 4–5). Use the highest fulfilled tier; the four-point cap still applies.


- **Architectural Zoo (004):** connected means uncovered and beside a covered space. For full coverage count building spaces, excluding water/rock.
- **Conservation Zoo (005):** count project supports by missing left-map tokens.
- **Naturalists' Zoo (006):** empty building spaces include upgrade-restricted spaces even if Build was not upgraded, but exclude water/rock.
- **Biodiverse Zoo (009):** gain **1 conservation per animal category** for which your zoo has more icons than the player to your right, **maximum 4 conservation**. If they have none of a category, one icon of yours is enough to win that category.
- **Map 1, Observation Tower:** its bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not just another rock hex. Housing an animal there gives the two appeal again after an earlier animal was released. Special enclosures get no tower effect. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
- **Map 2, Outdoor Areas:** a standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex (not merely another water hex) counts as two spaces larger **for all purposes after placement**. This bonus cannot be ignored on release or transfer; a physical size-2 enclosure there is treated as size 4. No effect on special enclosures; the Outdoor Area is not a building.
- **Map 4, Commercial Harbor:** a building on its adjacent building space connects/activates it. Your first building may start beside the Harbor, but need not. Its discard ability may be used before, during or after your action, only once per own turn; never during breaks or another player's turn. The Harbor is not a building.
- **Map 5, Park Restaurant:** break income is one money per adjacent **covered hex**, regardless of building type, occupancy or several hexes belonging to one building. The Restaurant is not a building. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives **one Reptile House or one Large Bird Aviary** free, even before Build II. Choose one, not both, and follow the other normal placement rules.
- **Map 6, Research Institute:** a building on its adjacent building space activates it; your first building may begin there but need not. Thereafter ignore one Animal-card condition, including one required icon or the Animals upgrade. All other conditions and all terrain requirements remain. The Institute is not a building.
- **Map 7, Ice Cream Parlors:** once all printed **kiosk placement-bonus spaces** are covered, every kiosk gives one extra money each break, whether built free or normally, even with no normally qualifying neighbors.
- **Map 8, Hollywood Hills:** cover H spaces by placing buildings under the ordinary placement rules. When an H is covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears; keep it and discard the others. H is not a placement bonus (so does not trigger Archaeologist). After covering all three, every Sponsor's level is one lower. Its bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner; bonus buildings still require Build II to cover upgrade-marked spaces.

### Official base FAQ

**Bonus icons:** an indicated size-2 or size-3 standard-enclosure bonus immediately builds that enclosure once for free, following ordinary placement and map-upgrade restrictions. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one requirement from a card's left edge; it does not remove terrain requirements. A special-enclosure symbol used as an immediate effect builds that indicated enclosure free. Take icons for money, reputation, conservation, X-tokens and workers in their shown quantities; worker activation follows the reserve order.


- A bonus granting a partner zoo or university takes an **available Association-board tile**, not one directly from general supply. A third/fourth partner requires Association II from any source; upgrade-restricted building spaces require Build II even with free buildings or Sponsors.
- A bonus letting you pay money to play a Sponsor costs money equal to that Sponsor’s level and requires its usual play conditions. Play it **only from hand**, even if Sponsors is upgraded. This paid-Sponsor effect leaves the Sponsors Action card in its current slot; it does not move it.
- A left-side **maximum 25 appeal** condition permits play only while your zoo has at most 25 appeal. The matching marker at appeal 25 is a reminder, not a general track cap. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least its printed reputation value. An Animal partner-zoo condition means a partner from its continent; a Sponsor partner-zoo condition permits any continent.
- Appeal cannot exceed **113**, nor conservation **41**; gains beyond those ends are lost. Reputation has its own overflow rule described above.

**The two end triggers give different final turn sets:** an end triggered at the end of a player's own turn gives every other player one final turn; an end triggered during a break gives every player one final turn. A normal break alone does not give any extra turns.

## Player Reference

- **Your turn:** pick 1 of your 5 Action cards → perform it at its slot's strength (1–5, +1 per X-token spent beforehand) → move it to slot 1, sliding the cards left of its slot one step right.
- **The 5 actions (side I → side II):**
  - **CARDS:** advance Break token 2; draw from deck per table (max 3, maybe discard 1), or snap 1 display card at strength 5+ → also draw within reputation range; snap from strength 3; reputation past 9 unlocked.
  - **BUILD:** 1 building, size ≤ strength, 2 money/space (kiosk, pavilion, standard enclosure, Petting Zoo) → several *different* buildings, total size ≤ strength; adds Reptile House & Large Bird Aviary and the restricted map spaces; full map = +7 appeal.
  - **ANIMALS:** play animals from hand per table (conditions → cost, −3/icon with matching partner zoo → empty enclosure of required size → effects) → also from display (pay folder number); at strength 5+, +1 reputation first.
  - **ASSOCIATION:** exactly 1 task (worker required; strength ≥ task value): +2 reputation / partner zoo / university / conservation project work → multiple different tasks, total value ≤ strength, plus max 1 donation (smallest visible amount, +1 conservation point).
  - **SPONSORS:** play 1 Sponsor card (strength ≥ level) OR advance Break token = strength and take that much money → play multiple (strength +1 ≥ total levels), also from display; break option pays double money.
  - **X-TOKEN (always available):** move a card to slot 1 and take 1 X-token (impossible with 5 X-tokens held).
- **Costs & limits:** buildings cost size × 2 money · max 1 each of Petting Zoo / Reptile House / Large Bird Aviary · kiosks ≥3 spaces apart · max 4 partner zoos (3rd needs upgraded Association) · hand limit 3 (5 with university), checked only at breaks · max 5 X-tokens.
- **Break:** discard to hand limit → clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens → recall workers, restock zoos/universities → discard display folders 1–2 and refill → income (appeal money + 1 money per building adjacent to each kiosk [occupied standard enclosures, special enclosures, pavilions, unique buildings] + break-income icons) → reset Break token.
- **Upgrades (4, choose wisely):** Conservation track space 2 (or extra worker) · Reputation track · 2nd partner zoo · 2nd university.
- **Game end:** at end of your own turn or during a break, your Appeal and Conservation counters in the same scoring area (or crossed) → finish turn, everyone else gets one more turn (during a break: everyone gets one more turn).
- **Score:** discard a Final Scoring card if no one hit 10 conservation points → score end-game cards and Final Scoring cards (max 4 conservation points each) → **VP = Appeal − lowest Appeal value in your Conservation counter's scoring area**. Highest positive VP wins; ties: most conservation projects supported, then shared victory.
